overview: Ireland is an island country in north-western Europe. It covers most of the island of Ireland; the north-east of the island is Northern Ireland, which is part of the United Kingdom. Its capital and largest city is Dublin. Ireland became independent from the United Kingdom in the 1920s and joined what is now the European Union in 1973. Irish and English are both official languages.

geography.text: Ireland is often called the Emerald Isle because of its green fields, kept lush by frequent rain from the Atlantic. The centre of the island is a low plain of farmland, lakes and peat bogs, ringed by coastal hills and mountains. The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and in the British Isles, and the rugged west coast includes the Cliffs of Moher.

history.text: Christianity reached Ireland in the 400s, and its monasteries became famous centres of learning. English, and later British, rule tightened from the 1100s onwards. The Great Famine of the 1840s killed about a million people and forced another million to emigrate. After the Easter Rising of 1916 and a war of independence, most of Ireland became independent in 1922.

events.title: Christianity arrives
events.text: Saint Patrick is traditionally credited with bringing Christianity to Ireland.

events.title: Anglo-Norman invasion
events.text: Anglo-Norman forces land in Ireland, beginning centuries of English rule.

events.title: Great Famine
events.text: Potato blight causes a famine that kills about a million people.

events.title: Easter Rising
events.text: Irish republicans rebel against British rule in Dublin.

events.title: Good Friday Agreement
events.text: A peace deal is agreed for Northern Ireland.
